body:
Quiet day on the arbitrage side: the scanner found zero cross-platform opportunities across all 80 live gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket. Nothing clears the combined spread-plus-fee hurdle, which is the normal outcome -- genuine riskless mismatches between these venues are rare and close fast when they appear.

The bigger story is how high gold has run. Spot sits in the $4,400-4,500 area, reflected in contract pricing: Kalshi's Above $4,410.99 settle contract for Sept 30, 2026 prices near 53-55 cents, while Polymarket's touch low $4,400 in September contract is bid at 0.89, implying traders see it as very likely gold has already dipped through that level this month. Reporting has gold near $4,521 per troy ounce on September 4, up sharply from about $4,331 three days earlier. Part of the move ties to a concrete military escalation between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz that pushed futures higher, on top of ongoing Fed rate-path uncertainty.

One note for readers scanning the raw tables: a few far-out-of-the-money year-end Kalshi strikes look slightly out of order, with the $5,400 or above contract bid above the adjacent $5,300 or above strike. That's not a real edge -- it reflects thin volume at those strikes (several show zero 24-hour volume), where spreads are wide enough to produce apparent inversions. Some Polymarket weekly touch contracts likewise show 80-cent-plus bid-ask gaps, a sign of an illiquid book rather than a tradable mispricing.
headline: No arbitrage across 80 gold contracts as spot price runs to $4,400-4,500
